title: S&P Reviews Nvidia Credit Rating Over Governance Concerns
summary: S&P Global Ratings considers downgrading Nvidia's AA credit rating to AA- citing governance issues and key man risk following CEO drama.
body_markdown:
**Officially launched on November 25, 2026.**


#### 💡 TL;DR


- S&P Global Ratings announced a review that could downgrade Nvidia's credit rating from AA to AA- within 90 days.
- The review cites governance weaknesses and key man risk following Jensen Huang's temporary ouster and reinstatement as CEO.
- A downgrade would increase Nvidia's borrowing costs and affect $500 billion in AI infrastructure financing guarantees.


S&P Global Ratings officially launched a review on November 25, 2026 that could result in Nvidia's credit rating dropping from AA to AA-, marking a rare governance-driven downgrade for one of the AI industry's most financially robust companies. The rating agency cited weak executive oversight, inadequate succession planning, and heavy dependence on CEO Jensen Huang following his controversial ouster and rapid reinstatement earlier this year.


The review positions Nvidia's strong balance sheet against persistent concerns about leadership stability and corporate governance at a moment when the company underwrites hundreds of billions in AI infrastructure financing. The outcome will shape borrowing costs across the AI supply chain for years to come.


## Release Date and Review Timeline


Officially announced on November 25, 2026, S&P's review will conclude within 90 days. The agency expects to complete its assessment by late February 2027, giving Nvidia one quarter to address governance concerns before a potential downgrade takes effect. This timeline coincides with Nvidia's fiscal year-end reporting period, when the company typically provides updated guidance on capital allocation and strategic priorities.


S&P emphasized that Nvidia will maintain its investment-grade rating regardless of the review outcome. The potential shift from AA to AA- keeps the company in the fourth-highest tier on the agency's scale, well above the BBB threshold that separates investment-grade from speculative debt.


## Governance and Key Man Risk Concerns


The rating review centers on two interconnected governance issues. First, S&P identified what it calls weak executive oversight mechanisms that allowed the board to remove and reinstate Huang without clear public explanation or strategic rationale. This opacity suggests potential conflicts between Huang's vision and board-level risk management priorities.


Second, the agency highlighted key man risk, the vulnerability created when a company's future depends disproportionately on a single executive. Despite Huang's undeniable track record in building Nvidia into a $3 trillion market-cap leader, S&P argues that no succession plan has been articulated publicly. The lack of identified internal candidates or transition framework creates uncertainty for long-term creditors.


These governance gaps contrast sharply with Nvidia's operational excellence. The company dominates AI chip production, maintains industry-leading margins, and shows no signs of financial distress. S&P's review reflects rare non-financial credit factors overriding strong balance-sheet fundamentals.


## Impact on AI Infrastructure Financing


A downgrade would immediately affect Nvidia's ambitious $500 billion AI infrastructure financing initiative announced in August 2026. The program involves six major financial institutions, including Goldman Sachs, Apollo, and Blackstone, with Nvidia guaranteeing 25% of loans to neoclouds and infrastructure companies lacking standalone credit strength.


Bloomberg reported that lenders had already pushed for larger guarantee percentages before the CEO drama unfolded. A lower Nvidia rating would likely trigger renegotiation clauses, forcing the company to backstop 35% to 40% of loans or accept higher interest rates on the entire facility. This would tie up more of Nvidia's capital in contingent liabilities rather than chip production or R&D investments.


Neocloud operators who rely on Nvidia-backed financing face the most direct consequences. Many of these startups lack the credit history to secure affordable debt independently. If Nvidia's guarantee becomes more expensive, their borrowing costs rise proportionally, potentially slowing infrastructure buildout across the AI ecosystem.


## Market and Competitive Context


Nvidia's credit review arrives as competitors including AMD, Intel, and emerging AI chip startups seek to capture market share. While none match Nvidia's scale or ecosystem lock-in today, prolonged governance uncertainty could create openings for rivals to position themselves as more stable long-term partners for hyperscalers and enterprise buyers.


The review also tests whether financial markets separate operational performance from governance quality. Nvidia's stock has remained resilient despite leadership turbulence, suggesting equity investors prize Huang's return over structural governance improvements. Credit markets typically take a longer view, prioritizing predictability and institutional continuity over charismatic leadership.


## What This Means


S&P's review forces Nvidia to address governance blind spots that financial success had papered over. The company must demonstrate credible succession planning and strengthen board oversight to preserve its AA rating and maintain favorable financing terms for the AI infrastructure ecosystem it anchors. For the broader AI industry, the episode underscores that even the most dominant players face credit scrutiny when leadership stability comes into question. The 90-day review period will reveal whether Nvidia treats governance as a compliance exercise or a strategic imperative worthy of the same rigor it applies to chip design.
